recs.stt: Flatten the Curve of Armchair Epidemiology
recs.x:
As far as I can tell the field that resembles epidemiology most closely is actually video game programming. The models epidemiologists vary in their approach, but the most advanced ones attempt to simulate society by simulating the interactions between people. That's why they can take into account things like school closures or novel social policies. 3Blue1Brown has done a good video where he implements an epidemiological model:

 [link]

He also had a nice video about epidemics/pandemics:
 [link]

The most simple models just assume that everyone meets everyone randomly. It's more complicated if you want to consider a more realistic model of how people move. For a decision about lockdown you need the complex model, but to understand herd immunity the simple model is good enough.

For a nice explanation of more complicated models, there is a video of 3Blue1Brown: "Simulating an epidemic" [link] Note that he explains that the models in this video are not 100% accurate, some number are chosen to get nice graphics, they are only useful to get some insight but not get quantitative predictions

recs.stt: India’s second wave of Covid-19 feels nothing like its first
recs.x:
Dynamics of the virus spread is quite interesting.

3Blue1Brown made a fascinating video about how an epidemic spreads: [link]

I know this is a controversial topic, but it shouldn’t be. This is a clear case that the science of pandemic modeling suggested one path and for political reasons we were pushed to follow a course that caused a lot of damage, some irreversible, to the society.
